title: As a developer, I can get a machine-learning risk score for a transaction in real time — synchronously, before authorization completes — through a documented API
As an ops user, I can map score ranges to actions — allow, review, block, step-up 3DS — and tune thresholds to my own risk appetite instead of a fixed cutoff
As a developer, I can feed the model my own signals — device fingerprints, behavioral data, custom metadata — so scoring reflects my business, not just network defaults
As a founder, scoring benefits from a cross-merchant network — a card or identity seen across thousands of other businesses informs the risk decision on mine
As a risk analyst, I can author custom rules that combine model scores, velocity counters, list matches, and transaction attributes into allow, block, or review decisions
As a risk analyst, I can backtest a rule against my historical traffic before deploying it, seeing exactly what it would have blocked, flagged, and cost
As an ops user, I can maintain allow and block lists — emails, cards, devices, IPs — and velocity limits, managed through the dashboard and programmatically
As a risk analyst, flagged transactions land in a review queue that shows the full context — customer history, signals, similar cases — so I can decide quickly and consistently
As an ops user, review work is a team workflow — assignment, escalation, SLAs, and a decision audit trail that shows who approved what and why
As a risk analyst, my review decisions and confirmed fraud outcomes feed back into the model and rules, so the system learns from every case we work
As a finance lead, I can shift fraud liability to the vendor — a chargeback guarantee that reimburses approved-then-disputed orders, with clear coverage terms
As an ops user, chargeback responses are automated — evidence compiled from order, delivery, and session data and submitted to the issuer without manual copy-paste
As a finance lead, I can see the numbers that matter — dispute rate, false-positive rate, approval-rate lift, review workload — and export them for the board
As a risk analyst, every score comes with its top risk factors — why this transaction looks risky — not just an opaque number
As a finance lead, I can measure the model itself — precision and recall on my traffic, shadow-mode trials of new models or rules before they take over decisions
As an ops user, I can control where fraud data lives and how long it's kept — regional residency options and retention controls that survive a privacy review
As a developer, European traffic is routed intelligently through SCA — 3DS triggered when required or risky, exemptions requested when safe — to protect both compliance and conversion
As an AI-native user, an agent can read my fraud posture and manage rules and lists programmatically — propose a velocity rule, update a blocklist — with human approval gates
As an AI-native user, an agent can work the review queue — pull flagged cases with their context, summarize the evidence, and recommend a decision for a human to confirm
As a risk analyst, the product ships its own AI assistant — natural-language queries over my fraud data, drafted rules, investigation summaries — built into the console
As a developer, I can use the product across whatever payment stack I run — multiple PSPs, gateways, and platforms — rather than being locked to one processor's rails
As an ops user, there are maintained integrations for my commerce stack — Shopify, Salesforce Commerce, BigCommerce, and the major PSPs — not just a raw API
As a risk analyst, protection extends beyond checkout — account takeover, fake account creation, promo and policy abuse are scored and managed in the same system
As an AI-native user, the product distinguishes malicious bots from legitimate AI buying agents, so agent-driven purchases aren't blanket-blocked as fraud
As a developer, I can pass verified agent identity — agentic-payment protocols, signed agent tokens, delegated spending scopes — into the risk decision as a first-class signal
